\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عاجل} (ʿājil)}{عاجل (ʿājil)}]{\ar{عاجل} (ʿājil) — urgent; breaking news}

\label{lesson:AR-C355-ajil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a flame, then the Arabic for to leak.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عاجل}}
\textbf{\ar{عاجل}} — \emph{ʿājil} — \textquotedblleft{}urgent; breaking news\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{قطع} \ar{التلفاز} \ar{البرنامج} \ar{لخبر} \ar{عاجل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{qaṭaʿa at-tilfāz al-barnāmaj li-khabar ʿājil.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The television interrupted the programme for breaking news.
\end{quote}

\ar{خبر} \ar{عاجل}: breaking news.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عاجل}} (\emph{ʿājil}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-j-l} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to hasten\textquotedblright{}, the root of the taught \emph{mustaʿjil}, in a hurry. \emph{ʿĀjil} is \textquotedblleft{}what comes quickly\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿājil}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿājil}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qaṭaʿa at-tilfāz al-barnāmaj li-khabar ʿājil.} — The television interrupted the programme for breaking news.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a flame, then the Arabic for to leak, then say \emph{ʿājil} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{عاجل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Urgent; breaking news\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مدونة} (mudawwana)}{مدونة (mudawwana)}]{\ar{مدونة} (mudawwana) — a blog}

\label{lesson:AR-C355-mudawwana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to leak, then the Arabic for urgent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مدونة}}
\textbf{\ar{مدونة}} — \emph{mudawwana} — \textquotedblleft{}a blog\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تكتب} \ar{أختي} \ar{مدونة} \ar{عن} \ar{الطبخ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taktubu ukhtī mudawwana ʿan aṭ-ṭabkh.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My sister writes a blog about cooking.
\end{quote}

Also a code of law: \ar{مدونة} \ar{الأسرة}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مدونة}} (\emph{mudawwana}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{d-w-n} (Lane), where \emph{dawwana} is \textquotedblleft{}to write into a register\textquotedblright{}, a \emph{dīwān}. \emph{Mudawwana} is \textquotedblleft{}a thing written down\textquotedblright{}; the blog is its modern sense.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mudawwana}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mudawwana}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taktubu ukhtī mudawwana ʿan aṭ-ṭabkh.} — My sister writes a blog about cooking.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to leak, then the Arabic for urgent, then say \emph{mudawwana} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مدونة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A blog\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تعليق} (taʿlīq)}{تعليق (taʿlīq)}]{\ar{تعليق} (taʿlīq) — a comment; a commentary}

\label{lesson:AR-C355-taliq}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for urgent, then the Arabic for a blog.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تعليق}}
\textbf{\ar{تعليق}} — \emph{taʿlīq} — \textquotedblleft{}a comment; a commentary\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كتب} \ar{القراء} \ar{تعليقات} \ar{كثيرة} \ar{على} \ar{المقال}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kataba al-qurrāʾ taʿlīqāt kathīra ʿalā al-maqāl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Readers wrote a lot of comments on the article.
\end{quote}

A sports commentator is \ar{معلق}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تعليق}} (\emph{taʿlīq}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-l-q} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to hang\textquotedblright{}, the root of the taught \emph{ʿallaqa}. A comment hangs on what was said.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʿlīq}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kataba al-qurrāʾ taʿlīqāt kathīra ʿalā al-maqāl.} — Readers wrote a lot of comments on the article.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for urgent, then the Arabic for a blog, then say \emph{taʿlīq} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تعليق} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A comment; a commentary\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{افتتاحية} (iftitāḥiyya)}{افتتاحية (iftitāḥiyya)}]{\ar{افتتاحية} (iftitāḥiyya) — an editorial}

\label{lesson:AR-C355-iftitahiyya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a blog, then the Arabic for a comment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{افتتاحية}}
\textbf{\ar{افتتاحية}} — \emph{iftitāḥiyya} — \textquotedblleft{}an editorial\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{قرأ} \ar{أبي} \ar{افتتاحية} \ar{الصحيفة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{qaraʾa abī iftitāḥiyyat aṣ-ṣaḥīfa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father read the newspaper’s editorial.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{افتتاحية}} (\emph{iftitāḥiyya}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-t-ḥ} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to open\textquotedblright{}, the root of the taught \emph{fataḥa}. The editorial is the piece that opens the paper.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a blog, then the Arabic for a comment, then say \emph{iftitāḥiyya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{نفى} (nafā)}{نفى (nafā)}]{\ar{نفى} (nafā) — to deny officially; to exile}

\label{lesson:AR-C355-nafa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a comment, then the Arabic for an editorial.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{نفى}}
\textbf{\ar{نفى}} — \emph{nafā} — \textquotedblleft{}to deny officially; to exile\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{نفت} \ar{الوزارة} \ar{الخبر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nafat al-wizāra al-khabar.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The ministry denied the report.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينفي}, \emph{yanfī}.

Also to exile: \ar{نفي}, exile. In grammar \ar{النفي} is negation.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{نفى}} (\emph{nafā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-f-y} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to drive away, to banish\textquotedblright{}. To deny a report is to drive it away.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nafā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nafā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nafat al-wizāra al-khabar.} — The ministry denied the report.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a comment, then the Arabic for an editorial, then say \emph{nafā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{نفى} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To deny officially; to exile\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
